content.title: About
content.content: Low‑fat cottage cheese with reduced lactose is a dairy product made from skimmed milk in which most of the lactose has been removed. It has a mild, slightly tangy flavor, a soft curdled texture and low calorie content, making it popular among weight‑watchers and people sensitive to lactose.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cottage cheese is one of the oldest dairy foods, known already in ancient Egypt.
Low‑fat versions contain about 90 % water, making them lighter than regular cottage cheese.
Lactose reduction is achieved by enzymatic hydrolysis, splitting lactose into glucose and galactose.
Cottage cheese is widely used in cheese‑nibbles, baked dishes and diet desserts.
In some countries the product is called “cottage cheese,” although texture may vary slightly.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Low‑fat cottage cheese provides roughly 12 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Fat usually does not exceed 1 %, making it suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Reduced lactose
items.content: The lower lactose level eases digestion for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: It supplies about 10 % of the daily calcium requirement, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to casein or whey proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain varieties are salted, so sodium intake should be monitored.

items.title: Processing quality
items.content: Low‑quality products may harbor microbial contamination; choose reputable brands.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cottage cheese can be enjoyed as a snack, blended into smoothies, added to salads, used as a filling for pancakes, casseroles and diet desserts. It pairs well with berries, nuts or a drizzle of honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C. Once opened, keep for 5–7 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.

content.title: About
content.content: The cheeseburger slider is a miniature version of the classic cheeseburger, consisting of a small bun, a beef patty, melted cheese, pickles, onion and sauce. It is perfect for a quick snack, buffet service, or as part of a mixed appetizer platter.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sliders first appeared in the United States in the early 1980s as a fast way to serve several small burgers.
The mini size allows for creative flavor combos, such as adding bacon or fried onions.
A single slider typically weighs 40–60 g, making it popular in kids' meals and diet menus.
They are often served in sets of three, simplifying calorie counting.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The beef patty provides high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Iron content
items.content: Red meat is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Melted cheese adds calcium that supports bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and cheese supply B12, B6 and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low carbohydrate count
items.content: The mini bun contains relatively few carbs, making the slider suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Cheese and beef can be high in saturated fat, which may raise cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Sauce and pickles add salt, potentially contributing to high blood pressure.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy should choose dairy‑free cheese alternatives.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improper storage of cooked sliders can lead to bacterial growth; keep them at safe temperatures.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the cheeseburger slider hot, usually on paper or cardboard trays. It is easy to eat with hands, paired with sauce, french fries, or fresh vegetable sticks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep prepared sliders in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight container for up to 3 months. Reheat before serving to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

content.title: About
content.content: Lentil soup is a nourishing dish made from red or green lentils, vegetables, broth, and spices. Lentils are rich in protein, fiber, and micronutrients, and the soup format makes these nutrients easy to digest.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lentils are one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown for over 8,000 years.
There are more than 50 lentil varieties, differing in color and flavor.
Lentil soup is a staple in many Middle Eastern and Mediterranean cuisines.
Lentils contain almost twice the protein of most other legumes.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Lentils provide essential amino acids, making them valuable for vegetarians and vegans.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar.

items.title: Contains iron and folate
items.content: These micronutrients are important for blood formation and anemia prevention.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Lentil soup raises blood glucose slowly, which is beneficial for people with diabetes.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phytonutrients in lentils help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to lentils.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Lentils contain oligosaccharides that can cause bloating in sensitive people.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid may reduce mineral absorption; soaking lentils before cooking can mitigate this.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve lentil soup hot, often finished with a splash of lemon juice, fresh herbs, or a drizzle of olive oil. It keeps well in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and can be frozen for longer storage.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared soup in an airtight container in the fridge for no more than 3 days. For longer keeping, portion it into freezer‑safe bags and freeze up to 2 months.
